text: Depending restructuring settings, distribution amplitude positive negative scoring bins affected. scoring procedure used TropFishR follows FiSAT II, outlined Gayanilo Pauly (1997). given set VBGF parameters, yearly repeating growth curves drawn lfq data. Scoring based concept “peaks”, runs positive negative scoring bins. peak takes value largest absolute value contained within. sum positive peaks called “available sum peaks” (ASP), represents maximum possible score (negative bins crossed). “estimated sum peaks” (ESP) sum peak values crossed growth curves, caveat positively crossed bins counted (.e. “flagged ”) negatively crossed bins counted every time hit (Pauly 1985). Finally, measure relative fit, ratio two values used calculate “new R” (Rn), can maximum value 1.0: Rn=10(ESP/ASP)/10Rn = 10^{(ESP/ASP)}/10 following plot, background shading shows runs peaks, positive peaks blue, negative peaks red, values zero white.  ELEFAN, time used rather age, point growth curve crosses length zero referred “anchor time” (t_anchor). interpreted time length equals zero. plot,t_anchor = 0.5, corresponds halfway year (.e. July 1st). Likewise, meaning ts slightly different; time year growth turns positive. ways, shift towards time perspective can help provide important biological information (.e. identify season growth strongest). Furthermore, back-calculation length zero across bins allows reconstruction relative recruitment index (see ?recruitment).

title: TropFishR 1.2.1
code: - The ELEFAN functions did not overwrite any element of the lfq object but instead   concatinated parameters onto the object. This can have unintended side effects, e.g. if several   growth parameters are saved in the lfq object and the plotting functions are called.   Now, the application of ELEFAN functions overwrites any growth parameters in the lfq object.

title: TropFishR 1.2
code: - Due to more efficient matrix computations ELEFAN is 2-4 times faster as before   - missing seed values were added in ELEFAN_GA()   - `plot.lfq()` allows plotting relative frequencies, this is   in particular useful in cases where one sampling time has a large number of samples   - `plot.catchCurve()` allows plotting results according to length rather   than relative age. This can be done with the argument `xaxis`.   - lfq plot can be used to plot 2 different lfq data sets; this allows to visually compare the two data sets   - `lfqModfiy()` allows combining two different lfq data sets. This   might be interesting when different fleets are investigated separately   - possible to define and plot multiple regression lines   in the catch curve analysis   - length converted catch curve can account for the seasonalized VBGF

title: TropFishR 1.2
code: - better control over graphical devices with par(),   when par() defined the default settings are not used   - growth parameters can now be added to lfq lists as "par" elements, this   is convenient as it is in line with the results of the ELEFAN methods
